operations.comment: ; Fixed-ROM consumer contracts (CPU addresses in physical banks 14/15).
; These names identify referenced fields within preserved payload blocks; they do not classify new bytes.
; Three 16-byte CHR cursor patterns.
; Eight masks select individual CHR bits.
; Eight inverse masks clear individual CHR bits.
; Eight-byte overlays indexed by pixel_color*8; applied to both paint planes.
; Eight little-endian pointers. Each descriptor begins with ten paint-pattern pointers, followed by four PPU colors at offsets 20..23 and six animated colors at offsets 24..29.
; High-byte view of the little-endian palette pointer table.
; 32 PPU palette bytes.
; Six colors indexed by accent_cycle_index.
; Four-byte records; consumer reads X, Y and paint selection at offsets 0..2 and advances by four.
; Y field in attract_point_records.
; Paint field in attract_point_records.
; Four one-bit channel masks.
; Pitch-indexed high bytes for APU timer periods.
; Pitch-indexed low bytes for APU timer periods.
; Instrument-indexed source bits for APU channel control.
; Instrument-indexed sweep source bits.
; Instrument-indexed sweep period source bits.
; Instrument-indexed sweep shift source bits.
; Fixed-volume values for instruments without an envelope.
; Initial pitch-effect phase per instrument.
; Per-update period adjustment.
; Pitch-phase timer reload.
; Zero selects fixed volume; nonzero enables envelope phases.
; Control bit source used while constructing channel control.
; Initial envelope timer.
; Envelope rise increment modulo sixteen.
; Envelope hold timer reload.
; Envelope decay decrement modulo sixteen.
; Release interval subtracted from note duration, then used as release-stage timer.
; Release decrement modulo sixteen.
; Sound ID indexes little-endian pointers; each descriptor contains four little-endian channel stream pointers, zero meaning retain that channel.
; Sixteen lower-16-KiB mapper values, indexed by picture.
; Sixteen low map-pointer bytes; corresponding high bytes at picture_map_high_table.
; Sixteen high map-pointer bytes.
; Sixteen low pattern-pointer bytes.
; Sixteen high pattern-pointer bytes.
; Sixteen low X-list pointer bytes.
; Sixteen high X-list pointer bytes.
; Sixteen low Y-list pointer bytes.
; Sixteen high Y-list pointer bytes.
; Sixteen point counts; previous-point wrap subtracts one.
; Names are coherent static interpretations of consumers, not original symbols or runtime proof.
; point_mode is the nonzero coordinate-list gate ($4D); palette_rebuild_busy is the action gate set during swatch generation ($13).
; picture_pattern_count is the map-following byte used as the eight-byte-pattern copy count; exact authored asset format remains unresolved.
; Symbols describe CPU spaces, not physical ROM identities. Fixed code executes in physical 8 KiB banks 14/15.
; Channel arrays use four-byte strides; tile/pixel work arrays are parallel byte stacks.
; pixel_stack_x occupies low stack-page RAM; hardware stack growth shares that CPU page. No overflow safety is established.
; tile_changed also temporarily preserves a clicked color; transfer_pointer is shared by copy and continuation roles.
; RAM scratch is reused across foreground, NMI transfers and transitions; pointer names describe their dominant contract.
; Isolated tile-work helper reuses these bytes with its own input contract.
; The fade routines reuse this page as a 16-color staging buffer.
; iNES header: mapper 2, 128 KiB PRG, CHR RAM and vertical mirroring. Kept verbatim; no checksum/header repair.

; Disable rendering and sound, wait across vblank edges, then initialize dispatchers and load the opening screen. The switchable lower 16 KiB is selected explicitly before its graphics are read.
; Poll the vblank flag; the outer counter repeats the settling interval.
; Wait for the flag to clear before the next settling interval.
; Hide every OAM entry before enabling rendering.
; Configure a timed transition through the shared vblank dispatcher. The continuation is installed in transfer_pointer and follows immediately below.
; Begin the next opening fade; the transfer pointer carries the fade completion continuation. These transitions share foreground and NMI dispatch state.
; Upload the second opening screen from the currently selected lower PRG bank, upload cursor tiles and fade in toward the timed display.
; Hold the second screen for 160 timer ticks, then continue to the final opening fade.
; Fade out and continue at LoadOpeningPicture; foreground work stays idle during the transition.
; Install fixed picture map/pattern pointers, upload the screen, initialize palette targets and begin fade-in.
; Foreground work uses a RAM indirect continuation; it spins or runs a fill while NMI advances display and input state.
; Idle continuation returns to the dispatcher.
; Install the idle foreground continuation.
; Return through the common vblank display epilogue.
; Install the ordinary vblank continuation.
; Temporarily disable input work by selecting the display epilogue.
; IRQ handler only reenables interrupts and returns; no mapper IRQ service is established.
; Save CPU registers, count the frame, copy OAM and blank rendering while the selected vblank continuation updates PPU state.
; Poll the controller before running the selected input continuation.
; Restore rendering, scroll and NMI enable, then advance sound and restore interrupted registers.
; Read eight serial controller bits, combine the two low input lines, and compute newly pressed buttons. A stable held state repeats after 48 frames and then every 10 frames.
; Direction bits move by two pixels in freehand mode; point mode steps through paired coordinate lists only on trigger/repeat. Actions require the idle foreground continuation and no palette rebuild.
; Controller layout: A=$80, B=$40, Select=$20, Start=$10, Up=$08, Down=$04, Left=$02, Right=$01.
; Runtime5/6 observed initialized freehand movement and a completed visible fill after artificial timer shortcuts; natural progression into this state remains a separate coverage question.
; Point stepping has finished; update the cursor through the common input path.
; Clamp freehand Y at 8; point-mode movement uses the neighboring point helper.
; Check down input using the same held versus repeat policy.
; Clamp freehand Y below 232.
; Check left input and point-mode gate.
; Previous-point stepping rejoins the common cursor update.
; Clamp freehand X at 40.
; Check right input and point-mode gate.
; Clamp freehand X below 248.
; A starts fill only while the foreground dispatcher is idle and palette generation has finished.
; Install fill work as the foreground continuation; NMI remains responsible for PPU transfers.
; B advances the ten-entry paint selection and updates its source pattern and cursor sprite.
; Apply the wrapped paint selection.
; Start schedules a delayed screen transition when painting is idle.
; Disable input and schedule the shared delayed transition.
; Select cycles eight palette descriptors, rebuilds pattern swatches and refreshes the cursor.
; Begin the selected palette rebuild.
; Update the cursor sprite and animated palette before servicing queued tile transfers.

; A nonzero address high byte is the producer/consumer handshake. Write a modified 16-byte CHR tile first; then read a requested tile, discarding the buffered PPU read. Clear each request only after its transfer.
; Wait-free NMI side of the CHR read request.
; Resume the common display epilogue.
; The timed transition installs the picture menu, then returns to foreground dispatch.
; Advance paired X/Y lists; a zero next X wraps to entry zero. Input is ignored while fill or palette rebuild is active.
; Load both coordinates and retain their shared index.
; Step backward through paired point lists, wrapping with the per-picture point count.
; Read the selected paired coordinates.
; Write one OAM record using X as tile number and cursor coordinates minus eight. Sprite attributes are zero.

; Write the high and low nibbles of A as two OAM tiles at Y=10, X=5/13, with attributes zero. Restores A through shared transfer scratch. Actual caller and display purpose remain unresolved; this is a static helper contract.
; Copy three 16-byte patterns from fixed ROM into CHR RAM starting at PPU address zero.
; Three 16-byte cursor CHR patterns copied by UploadCursorPatterns; each tile contains two eight-row bitplanes.

; Unresolved generic data: twenty palette-valued bytes followed by four FF bytes. Nearby/reference inspection found no supported consumer or record schema; the following clear helper has an independent entry contract.
; Fill 1024 PPUDATA bytes with FF from PPU address $2000. Requires increment-one PPU configuration and suitable display timing; no caller or natural execution has been established.
; X wraps through 256 writes and Y counts four pages, covering one nametable plus its attribute area.
; Use A as both mapper value and ROM address offset. Bank-start bytes 0..7 provide bus-conflict-safe mapper writes; this changes the lower 16 KiB, not the fixed executing code.
; Save the fill origin, derive 8x8 tile coordinates, request its CHR data and read the clicked two-bit pixel. Check the replacement pattern before starting the tile/pixel work stacks.
; Foreground waits for NMI to finish an outstanding write.
; Foreground waits for NMI to fetch the requested tile.
; For higher paint selections, try zero as the match color while retaining the original clicked color.

; Use PatternContainsClickedColor carry: an absent candidate color chooses that fallback; otherwise try the next of three colors. Exhaustion restores the original paint selection through the existing exit.
; Construct two eight-byte plane pointers in the fixed fallback-pattern run, sixteen bytes apart per color. Carry propagation updates both high bytes.
; Mark this as a fallback selection and restore the clicked color before flood initialization.
; Seed the pixel stack, then process tile-boundary work until the tile stack is empty or cancellation is requested.
; Pop coordinates, edge mask and entry direction from parallel byte arrays. Their index is an eight-bit stack count.
; Convert edge-mask bits into seed pixels on the right boundary.
; Convert edge-mask bits into seed pixels on the left boundary.
; Convert edge-mask bits into seed pixels on the bottom boundary.
; Convert edge-mask bits into seed pixels on the top boundary.
; Run local pixel flood from the boundary seeds.
; Restore the selected paint pattern if the fill temporarily changed it.
; The saved paint choice is restored; rebuild its plane data through the shared preparation path.
; Return foreground dispatch to idle.
; Scan an 8x8 replacement pattern for the clicked two-bit color. Carry reports whether it occurs.

; Push one tile-flood work record unless its byte count is FF. A supplies the edge/direction field; $3F/$40/$41 supply X, Y and mask in this helper contract. The arrays match PopTileFloodWork. Actual caller remains unresolved.

; Clear four outgoing edge masks, fetch the tile and flood connected eligible pixels from the local stack. Changed tiles are queued for NMI writeback; outgoing edge masks seed adjacent tiles within the 32x30 map.
; Process local X/Y seeds until none remain.
; Send the edited tile to NMI; fully filled edge masks use the map-wide propagation path.
; Append neighboring tile work only when its edge mask is nonzero and it lies in bounds.
; Right neighbor is bounded at tile X 31.
; Top neighbor is bounded at tile Y zero.
; Bottom neighbor is bounded at tile Y 29.
; Commit the new tile-work count.

; Scan the 32x30 picture map for adjacent occurrences of the same tile number; shared CHR tiles can affect multiple map positions. When a neighbor uses the edited tile, enqueue the current cell with a full mask on the shared entry edge; continuations complete its work-array fields.
; Compare the current cell with the edited tile number.
; Inspect the left neighbor without crossing the row boundary.
; Queue the current cell from its left edge: finish Y, direction 1 and a full edge mask, then advance the work count.
; Inspect the right neighbor within the 32-column row.
; Queue the current cell from its right edge: finish Y, direction 0 and a full edge mask, then advance the work count.
; Inspect the preceding row only below row zero.
; Queue the current cell from its top edge: finish X, direction 3 and a full edge mask, then advance the work count.
; Inspect the following row only above row 29.
; Queue the current cell from its bottom edge: finish X, direction 2 and a full edge mask, then advance the work count.
; Advance the map pointer and column; wrap after 32 columns and stop after 30 rows.

; Treat color 3 as a boundary and skip pixels already equal to the replacement pattern. Otherwise paint the pixel and push its four neighbors; neighbors outside the tile accumulate outgoing edge masks.
; Record propagation through the left tile boundary.
; Record propagation through the right tile boundary.
; Record propagation through the top tile boundary.
; Record propagation through the bottom tile boundary.
; Return without further pixel work.
; Return the bit for the current boundary coordinate, preserving the stack index in Y.
; Calculate map pointer as base + tile_y*32 + tile_x. Read the tile number and request its 16-byte CHR pattern at $1000 + tile_number*16; wait for NMI to clear the request.
; Nonzero request high byte means NMI has not completed the read.
; Read a two-bit color from the two eight-byte planes in tile_buffer; X selects bit position and Y selects row.
; Replace the selected bit in both buffered planes using replacement_plane_a/b and mark the tile changed.
; Read the corresponding two-bit pixel from the selected paint pattern and expand its plane bits to all-zero/all-one replacement masks.
; Wait for an earlier write, then publish the tile address to NMI. The address high byte is the pending flag.
; Eight descending one-bit masks followed by eight complements. Pixel readers and writers index these with the within-tile X coordinate.
; Position the palette marker sprite at 20-pixel intervals for the ten paint choices.
; Load a little-endian pattern pointer from the palette descriptor. The second bitplane begins eight bytes after the first.
; Load the palette-set descriptor, preserve the selected paint and temporarily choose entry zero while NMI builds all swatch tiles.
; Write background/sprite palette entries with repeated background color; animated colors substitute two descriptor fields.
; Four eight-row swatch overlays, indexed by color 0..3; the builder applies each overlay to both CHR planes.
; Combine an eight-row paint pattern with the swatch overlay, writing both CHR planes. Destination depends on paint selection and two-bit color variant.
; Build two variants per frame, four per paint selection and ten selections total, then enable the palette display continuation.
; Clear the busy flag and switch foreground continuation to palette sprite setup.
; Restore paint selection and construct the repeated four-sprite swatches. Then enable painting input and palette animation.

; Snapshot frame_counter and return when it equals the saved A. Usually returns immediately. If NMI changes the counter between load and compare, this can wait for the saved byte to recur. Actual caller and intended timing purpose remain unresolved; this does not wait until the counter changes.
; Advance one descriptor color every ten calls and another color every two calls; each cycles six entries. Upload only after palette display is enabled.
; Write the fixed 32-byte palette to PPU palette RAM.
; Eight little-endian descriptor pointers, selected modulo eight. Targets reorder the eight records that follow.
; Eight 30-byte palette descriptors: ten little-endian paint-pattern pointers, four PPU colors at offsets 20..23, then six animated colors at offsets 24..29.
; Referenced planar paint patterns: each 16-byte tile has eight rows per plane; descriptor pointers select these fixed patterns.
; Two unselected 16-byte planar-looking blocks at $CCAB/$CCBB. Their neighboring patterns and bounded extent support generic data; no selector or authored use is established.
; Remaining referenced 16-byte paint patterns; fourteen tiles across both referenced runs are selected by descriptor pointers.
; Default 32-byte PPU palette copied by the default-palette loader.
; Six accent PPU colors, indexed by accent_cycle_index and wrapped at six.
; Hide all OAM shadow entries by writing $F8 through the page.
; Hide sprites, install a six-frame palette darkening continuation and return foreground work to idle.
; Every six frames subtract $10 from sixteen colors, clamping underflow to $0F. Once all are dark, jump through transfer_pointer to the next stage.
; Install the six-frame brightening continuation and initialize colors from the low nibbles of palette_target.
; Upload current colors and raise each by $10 toward its target. On completion jump through transfer_pointer.
; Copy 960 map bytes plus 64 zero attributes to the nametable. Read the following pattern count and expand each eight-byte source plane into both planes of a CHR tile.
; Clear the last CHR tile, then overwrite five tiles at the start of each of 30 nametable rows with $FF.
; Copy bytes through transfer_pointer to PPUDATA. X is the low byte count; Y supplies the remaining page count. Pointer increments across page boundaries.
; Copy 1024 nametable/attribute bytes, retain the following 16-color palette pointer, then read a pattern count and copy count*16 bytes to CHR RAM at $1000.
; Clear tile-transfer flags and initialize paint replacement state, then install the attract-mode input continuation.
; Run scripted point/color records until 43 have been consumed; a controller action requests cancellation once demonstration progress exists. Wait for foreground fill before transitioning.
; Defer cancellation while a fill is running.
; Read a four-byte record: X, Y, paint selection and one unconsumed byte. Schedule fill for the next point.
; Resume the ordinary vblank epilogue.
; Stop audio, prepare palette targets and schedule a fade-out transition.
; Upload the fixed menu map/patterns and fade in its initial palette.
; Set cursor and grid selection coordinates, start the menu sound, and install menu input.
; Install menu input and return foreground dispatch to idle.
; Direction triggers move the grid selection; row and column updates wrap within the four-by-four menu. A selects point mode and B freehand mode.
; Move one menu row up, wrapping row 0 to 3; the paired screen Y coordinate changes by 57 pixels.
; Check triggered down input and play its navigation sound.
; Move one menu row down, wrapping row 3 to 0 and restoring screen Y=50.
; Check triggered left input and play its navigation sound.
; Move one menu column left, wrapping column 0 to 3; screen X changes by 63 pixels.
; Check triggered right input and play its navigation sound.
; Move one menu column right, wrapping column 3 to 0 and restoring screen X=32.
; A chooses point-to-point mode.
; Continue menu epilogue after scheduling the picture.
; B chooses freehand mode. Start/Select tests currently converge on the same cursor update.
; Test Start before updating the menu cursor.
; Test Select before updating the menu cursor.
; Use tile 2 for the menu cursor and finish vblank.
; Combine grid row*4 + column, select the picture bank, play selection sound and schedule a 50-frame delay before fade-out.
; Stop sound and select the picture initialization continuation after fade-out.
; Load parallel per-picture pointer tables for map, patterns and paired point lists. Set a freehand default or the first point, upload picture and rebuild palette.
; Upload map/patterns, reserve palette area and begin fade-in.
; Start with paint selection zero and generate all palette swatches.
; Count down frames, copy the pending continuation into foreground dispatch and restore the ordinary vblank handler.
; Select a palette descriptor and stage its colors plus black fill entries in RAM for fades. The shared pointer now addresses the staged palette.
; 43 four-byte attract records. Consumer reads X, Y and paint selection at offsets 0..2 and advances by four; the fourth byte has no established meaning.
; Clear the software enable mask and disable APU channels.
; Initialize all four channel active flags and instrument zero before use.
; Read four little-endian stream pointers from the selected sound descriptor, replacing only nonzero channel streams and enabling those channels.
; Stream records are duration/value pairs. Commands: $00 terminates, $FF selects instrument, $FE restarts background_sound.
; Walk four channels in register strides of four. Fetch duration/value pairs as needed, handle stream commands, update pitch/envelope state and write APU registers.
; Fold the channel active flag into the hardware enable mask; skip channels absent from the software sound mask.
